text:
Maya Rivera: I'm taking over primary for the 18:00->02:00 UTC shift. oncall-bot just opened an incident for high p95 tail latency & intermittent 503s on hosted /v1/generate. initial spike at ~17:54 UTC. tagging infra/runtime/support/security to triage. runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/hosted-runtime-high-latency :wave:

oncall-bot: INCIDENT CREATED #INC-2026-1287 — High tail latency observed for hosted-runtime. pages: maya, omar. priority: P2. links: dashboard /alerts/hosted-runtime, logs /logs/hosted-runtime.

Maya Rivera: Quick context for folks — customers reporting increased 503s during medium-length (>512 tokens) requests only, single model-family (rwkv-97) shows largest error count. Support reported 12 active customers affected (see Alex's message below).

Omar Khan: looking now. first-pass: not a model failure, kernel logs show some CUDA OOMs on node pool gp2-us-west2. KV cache pressure also obvious in traces. running these locally to confirm:```bash
kubectl -n runtime get pods -l app=redwood-runtime
kubectl -n runtime logs <pod> --tail=200
kubectl top pod <pod>
```

Priya Desai: infra sees 3 nodes in gp2-us-west2 with repeated evictions around 17:50-17:55 UTC. Autoscaler didn't add capacity — policy is capped for this pool. I'm increasing pool cap to allow 2 more nodes now, ETA ~6m for nodes to come up. Also investigating kernel driver errors on one host.

Jin Park: preliminary security check — no obvious malicious patterns in headers or IPs, mostly legit client IPs. However, rate distribution shows a sudden bump of many small concurrent requests from a handful of customers which could amplify KV cache pressure. Suggest putting a temporary token-based soft-throttle for these tenants (support can notify them).

Alex Chen: support update — 12 customers impacted, 4 have higher volume (1 enterprise, 3 mid-market). Customers mostly report timeouts and retries. I've opened comms for the enterprise account (CS+AE looped). Will post standardized message in status page if this persists >30m.

Maya Rivera: routing/ownership note to avoid ping-pong: runtime owns model-level behavior, KV cache, and pod-level errors; infra owns node pool, autoscaler, and kernel driver issues; security owns anomalous traffic or abuse vectors; support owns customer comms. If a symptom crosses domains, coordinate but primary owner of the symptom is listed above.

Omar Khan: quick mitigation I'm rolling now: 1) enable per-request fallback to smaller model variant (rwkv-97 -> rwkv-32lite) for requests >512 tokens for affected route; 2) flush a subset of KV caches to free memory; 3) apply a short-term intra-region concurrency cap for that model to protect nodes. Applying step 1 now (will update when traffic shifts).

Priya Desai: nodes booting. Autoscaler cap increased +2. If OOMs persist after new nodes join, we should consider evicting heavy batch workers to a quieter pool.

Jin Park: I'll prepare a temporary WAF rule to identify the high-concurrency tenants and apply a soft throttle if needed. Will coordinate with Alex for affected tenant IDs.

Alex Chen: sharing the tenant IDs in DM to Jin. Also prepping a support template: "We're investigating intermittent timeouts on generation. We're applying mitigations and will update in 15m."

Maya Rivera: runbook pointer for on-call folks: /runbooks/hosted-runtime-high-latency has steps for checking kernel OOMs, evictions, and safe rollback to prior model variant. If you need the quick commands:```bash
# check pods with OOMKilled
kubectl -n runtime get pods -o wide | grep OOMKilled
# check node events
kubectl get events --sort-by='.lastTimestamp' -n runtime | tail -n 50
# trigger model fallback (internal API)
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \n  https://controlplane.local/api/v1/model-fallback -d '{"model":"rwkv-97","fallback":"rwkv-32lite","route":"/v1/generate"}'
```

Maya Rivera: Handoff plan: I'll remain primary until 02:00 UTC. Omar, can you take primary 02:00->10:00 UTC? Priya can be infra secondary for the window overnight; Jin will be on-call for security checks; Alex will handle customer comms. We have a potential coverage gap 05:00-06:00 UTC because on-call rotation doesn't currently have a dedicated infra person then — Priya, can you confirm if you can extend or if I should book a bridge with infra on-call? :thinking_face:

Omar Khan: I can take primary at 02:00. For the 05:00-06:00 gap, I can be on standby for infra-ish actions but prefer Priya to be primary infra. If Priya can't, we should escalate to the infra pager or prep escalation runbook lines.

Priya Desai: I can extend to cover 05:00-06:00 UTC today. Please note I'll be on a short call 03:40-04:10 UTC — Omar willing to step in then.

Maya Rivera: great — summary for posting to the incident channel: short bullet list of current state, mitigations applied, owners, and next shift coverage. I'll post in 5m once we confirm new nodes joined and error rate drops. If anything changes ping me directly. :lock: :gear: :telephone_receiver:

oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE #INC-2026-1287 — Mitigations applied: model fallback -> rwkv-32lite, autoscaler cap increased +2, temporary concurrency cap applied. Next update in 10m or on significant change.
